title: Trial-order grip change does not reliably improve cross-cohort prediction of digit-symbol performance beyond maximum strength
abstract: We tested whether information discarded by maximal grip summaries predicts concurrent cognitive performance. A bilateral normalized third-minus-first grip contrast augmented a conventional-measure spline ridge predictor of Digit Symbol Substitution Test (DSST) score. Training used NHANES 2011–2012 (n=924); frozen evaluation used separately recruited 2013–2014 (n=1056). Examination-weighted MSE increased from 165.066 to 168.909 DSST points squared, difference +3.843, joint source/target PSU-bootstrap 95% interval [-2.974, +20.774]. The registered improvement criterion failed. Subgroup and influence checks changed the point-estimate sign. This exploratory negative/inconclusive result establishes neither equivalence nor absence of cognitive information in repeated grip. Separate recruitment within NHANES is not independent-program validation.
